key_impacts: Large quantities of radioactive material were released to the environment.
Over three hundred thousand residents were evacuated from the vicinity.
Large stretches of land were rendered uninhabitable.
Cleanup will take decades and may cost hundreds of billions of dollars.
Tsunami inundation led to loss of emergency power and a station blackout.
evidence_snippets: The March 2011 accident at Japan’s Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station.
Large quantity of radioactive material released… over three hundred thousand residents evacuated.
About forty-five minutes after the earthquake, the station was inundated by tsunami waves… complete loss of AC power… station blackout.
Following a flooding incident at Blayais Nuclear Power Plant in France in 1999…
European countries significantly enhanced their plants’ defenses against extreme external events.
Chernobyl in 1986… led to significant releases of radiation.
Three Mile Island in 1979… extensive damage to nuclear fuel but a relatively small release of radiation.
